theme: catalogued line divisions, unsupervised segmentation and alternation
question: Do catalogued line divisions fall at recurring-unit boundaries, and do segmented Indus units show Kober-style stem alternation beyond readable comparison corpora?
outcome: Complete lines recur elsewhere more often than windows crossing the division: 23 faces against 4, with 42 ties, under the conservative line order (p = 0.0003). Results survive shifted-division, deduplication and numeral-line controls in review. The Dirichlet-process segmenter places a boundary at 76 of 76 divisions against 37% of other positions. Indus alternation (0.029) lies inside every matched comparison range and is descriptive.
challenge: Pooling both line orders biased the control. Interior lines were counted twice, boustrophedon faces were misread, and segmenter agreement was omitted.
remedy: Conservative order added in v2; v3 counts lines once and excludes boustrophedon faces; segmenter agreement computed in review.
retry_when: More boundary evidence from multi-line tablets or photograph-measured spacing permits supervised segmentation.
